notes: Fog-of-war regression suite. The DEFAULT pass captures the static grid-reveal scene (fog_zoom2/4/8_origin): a visible reveal circle, an explored memory band, and unexplored black, plus the #2008 column-cull pillar canary — the general FOG_TO_TRIXEL + per-voxel-column-clip guard. The 'edge' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-zoom (a static analytic vision circle at the origin with VOXEL objects straddling its boundary) and gates the fog CUT-FACE cross-section (#2125, epic #2124 P1): a boundary-cut voxel object caps with a filled interior wall instead of a see-through hole. The scene also carries a thick ground slab spanning the disc; its cut RIM gates the screen-space cross-section silhouette (#2124 follow-up): the own-column drop keeps the boundary cells the disc crosses (nearest-cell test) so FOG_TO_TRIXEL trims the rim to the analytic disc at game resolution instead of stair-stepping on the voxel lattice. The 'detached' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --detached-edge (the same origin vision circle but the boundary-straddling object is a world-placed DETACHED_REVOXELIZE solid on its own canvas + pool) and gates the detached cross-section (#2127, epic #2124 P3): a detached canvas carries no fog of its own, so this proves the world fog + observers thread into its STAGE_1/2 dispatch and each voxel's world column is recovered from worldCellOffset — it cross-sections like the GRID twin instead of rendering whole. The 'edge_smooth' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-smooth — the SAME geometry as --edge-zoom but a wide soft vision-circle band (Mode B, #2126 P2): the object silhouette + cut wall fade on the smooth disc curve like the floor (the own-column drop keeps partially-revealed columns so FOG_TO_TRIXEL trims them), rather than ending hard at the binary radius. The 'edge_sdf_blocker' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-sdf-blocker — the SAME --edge-zoom voxel scene PLUS one SDF box carrying C_LightBlocker{blocksLOS_=true} straddling the -Y disc arc (#2247): #2247 reported an SDF blocker's fog-hidden half black-banding the cut instead of capping. Master's geometric cut cap (#2274) is content-independent — the box's rendered surface caps at the disc boundary regardless of any occlusion bitfield, so its -Y half fills with the toned cut wall like the -X voxel slab. This is the ENABLED-path gate proving a blocksLOS_ SDF straddling the disc still caps (the cap does not special-case blockers) — a scene WITHOUT the box (the other runs) proves nothing about it. The 'edge_zcost' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-zcost — the vision disc as an XY radius with a Z-COST HEIGHT penalty (#2260): the observer sits at floor level, a central tall voxel pillar at the observer's XY has its base revealed and its top penalized past the disc (dist_xy + zCost*|z - observerZ|) so it fades then drops, and a low cube at the same XY band stays fully revealed. This is the ENABLED-path gate for the height penalty (every other run passes zCost 0, so they prove nothing about it); those other runs are the byte-identity gate that zCost 0 is a no-op. The 'edge_zcost_asym' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-zcost-asym — #2557's generalization to ASYMMETRIC up/down costs: an up pillar (same geometry as edge_zcost's) fades fast under the larger up-cost, and a SEPARATE short down-side block (its own, closer, XY offset — see the kEdgeZCostAsymDownXOffset comment in main.cpp for why it isn't a mirror of the up pillar's reach: the render cull's visible iso viewport is asymmetric in Z at this camera pose) stays mostly revealed under the much smaller down-cost. Positive-fire verified during implementation: forcing zCostDown to mirror zCostUp measurably shrinks/darkens the down block (img_diff ~1.1% drift concentrated in its ROI) versus the shipped asymmetric costs. The 'edge_zcost_ceiling' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --edge-zcost-ceiling — #2557's penalty-free height BAND + near-radius up-cost: the same edge_zcost pillar/cube geometry, but matter within the band reveals fully then cuts off within ~1 unit past it, a hard ceiling instead of a linear fade. Positive-fire verified during implementation: forcing freeBand to 0 nearly drops the pillar and cube entirely (img_diff ~35% drift) versus the shipped band-8 costs, which keep them mostly revealed. The zcost rows also gate the FIELD invariant: stage 1's world drop is z-free, so a height-hidden sample stays in the geometry and FOG_TO_TRIXEL paints it the unexplored colour (black by default) — the pillar keeps its full height and top face instead of a hollow shorter box with the floor behind it. The 'edge_zcost_ceiling_paint' EXTRA RUN re-runs --edge-zcost-ceiling with --fog-debug-color (unexplored colour magenta) so painted-hidden matter reads apart from the black background; the same run logs FOG-PAINT-PROBE (the central pillar's texel count and how many carry the debug colour). Its third shot, fog_edge_zcost_ceiling_paint_yaw9, parks a non-cardinal yaw (0.35 rad) so the scene renders through the per-axis rotation route, which FOG_TO_TRIXEL never paints: there the above-ceiling pillar voxels are dropped on the z-aware curve, so the pillar ends at the ceiling instead of rendering lit to full height. Positive-fire verified: with the per-axis drop made z-free, the pillar renders lit to its full 28-voxel height in that shot. The 'entity_reveal' EXTRA RUN re-runs with --entity-reveal — fog BODY subjects under the edge_zcost_ceiling band and up-cost: an untagged voxel pillar (adopted as a BODY within one frame) and a governed one render whole above the hard ceiling at one uniform factor (the entity-id fog BODY bit plus its 8-bit factor make FOG_TO_TRIXEL skip the field, the height terms, the rim fade and the cut cap for their pixels), a governed pillar straddling the disc rim renders whole too, a FIELD-tagged control column at the same anchor distance clips per sample (painted above the ceiling, rim fade on its outer columns), a flagged SDF box renders whole while its unflagged twin clips (shapes take the BODY route in a later child), a governed pillar outside every circle stays hidden, and an EXEMPT pillar (marker at construction) outside every circle renders whole. The same run logs FOG-BODY-PROBE per body: the after-fog / before-fog luminance ratio range over the body's texels, the texels above the ceiling, and the texels carrying the cut-face bit. The 'entity_reveal_soft' EXTRA RUN re-runs the same scene with --entity-reveal-soft-edge (edge softness 4): the rim pillar's anchor verdict lands inside the hysteresis band, so the whole body renders at one dimmed factor. Each extra run emits exactly its kEdgeShots/kDetachedEdgeShots/kEdgeSmoothShots/kEdgeSdfBlockerShots/kEdgeZCostShots/kEdgeZCostAsymShots/kEdgeZCostCeilingShots/kEdgeZCostCeilingPaintShots/kEntityRevealShots/kEntityRevealSoftShots, so capture_offset 0 maps them 1:1. All gated scenes except fog_edge_zcost_ceiling_paint_yaw9 are static + cardinal-yaw-0 with identity-rotation detached solids (the source re-voxelize path — a spinning solid round-to-cell speckles, #1557), verified bit-deterministic run-to-run on macOS (0 drift). The demo's other modes (--moving-observer orbit, --player-walk) are intentionally NOT gated here — they advance a per-frame float center, so they are non-deterministic by construction (manual / attach-screenshots inspection aids). Reference PNGs live in sibling subdirs per CMake preset (macos-debug/, linux-debug/) since Metal and OpenGL produce pixel-different output; linux-debug/ is captured on a Linux/OpenGL host (fleet:needs-linux-smoke) — a backend without committed references SKIPS rather than fails, so bless it there with render-verify --update-references. Shot order mirrors kShots[] / kEdgeShots[] / kDetachedEdgeShots[] / kEdgeSmoothShots[] / kEdgeSdfBlockerShots[] / kEdgeZCostShots[] / kEdgeZCostAsymShots[] / kEdgeZCostCeilingShots[] / kEdgeZCostCeilingPaintShots[] / kEntityRevealShots[] / kEntityRevealSoftShots[] in main.cpp.
